reason: Both retained objects (proposer and solver policies) are updated and persisted as model weights via HRPO/GRPO; no prompt/skill/tool/workflow/memory/evaluator/config is changed and retained (rubric A3). Per EVIDENCE.md weight-updating self-play/self-curriculum is excluded. Not scored; the paper is a coherent weight-training study, not a defect.

paper.title: Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data
paper.central_claim: Dr. Zero lets search agents self-evolve without curated QA training data: a proposer generating structurally diverse multi-hop questions and a solver, both initialized from the same base LLM, are co-trained with a difficulty-guided reward and HRPO, matching or surpassing supervised search agents (Search-R1) on several QA benchmarks at lower proposer-training cost.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker; configured type recorded only.

evidence.quote: the proposer is optimized via HRPO to produce verifiable, diverse and challenging queries. Meanwhile, the solver leverages the generated data through GRPO to refine its search and reasoning capabilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Both loop participants are updated by RL gradient steps; the improvement is in policy parameters.

evidence.quote: we train the proposer for 50 steps, generate QA data on the corresponding prompts, and subsequently utilize this data to train the solver for 50 steps via GRPO
evidence.support_explanation: Alternating weight training is the only persisted change; the generated QA data is a transient training batch, not a retained harness component.

evidence.quote: On single-hop tasks (i.e., NQ, TriviaQA and PopQA), our 3B model outperforms the supervised Search-R1 by 22.9%, 6.5% and 18.4% respectively.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported effect of the weight-trained agent; not an effect of a retained non-weight component.

signatures.object: proposer and solver LLM policies (Qwen2.5 3B/7B-Instruct weights)
signatures.information: search tool over Wikipedia E5 index; seed documents; solver pass rate k/n on proposer questions; no human questions or answers
signatures.operation: proposer rolls out multi-turn tool-use to produce a hop-n question+answer; solver attempts n=5 times; proposer reward = 1[0<k<n](n-k)/(n-1)+format; HRPO normalizes advantage within hop-count groups; solver trained with GRPO on proposer QA
signatures.output: updated proposer and solver weights per iteration (3 iterations)
signatures.conditions: short-form verifiable QA with a fixed Wikipedia corpus
signatures.feedback: solver pass rate on synthetic question; exact match against proposer-synthesized answer
signatures.selection_rule_data: reward band excludes k=0 and k=n; no held-out acceptance gate between iterations
signatures.later_use: next iteration's proposer/solver start from updated weights
signatures.claimed_effect: avg EM 0.326 (3B) / 0.372 (7B) vs Search-R1 0.327 / 0.384, higher than data-free R-Zero*/SQLM*
signatures.failure_boundary: plateau after 2-3 iterations; 7B instability from token-ID inconsistency; synthetic answers may be incorrect/ambiguous

gap.author_gap: Existing data-free self-evolution produces homogeneous one-hop questions and standard GRPO needs nested sampling that is too costly for multi-turn search agents.
gap.checked_gap: The author-stated gap is about question diversity and training compute of a weight-training loop; supported in paper by the 93.4%/95.6% one-hop share of SQLM*/R-Zero* generations (A.2).
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: R-Zero (proposer-solver co-evolution), SQLM (self-questioning), Search-R1 (supervised RL search agent); all weight-training.
gap.residue: Not a non-weight harness gap; no fixed non-weight component made editable.
gap.method_response: Hop-grouped baseline plus difficulty-guided reward cheapen and diversify proposer training.
gap.remaining_gap: Plateau after 2-3 iterations; reward hacking and bias amplification left to future work.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Signal is manufactured from the model's own proposer outputs and solver pass rate (generated-and-filtered synthetic samples); C26 preference-pair tactic not executed (reward is scalar RL, not pairwise preference); C08 confidence-cutoff pseudo-labeling is nearest but the retained loop here is a curriculum of tasks, so no sub card is asserted.
matches.success_failure_checks: Success: grounding via search tool and seed doc; failure: self-constructed answers may be wrong (acknowledged by authors).
matches.reason: Operation derives the training signal from model-generated questions filtered by solver pass-rate band.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary fit is partial; recorded for completeness since the paper is out_of_scope.

matches.condition_checks: rsi:self_generate_the_curriculum/S2 partial (pass-rate band is on solver rollouts, not a fixed held-out env); rsi:self_generate_the_curriculum/F1 mitigated by grounded-answer prompt but no independent validity check (acknowledged).

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Proposer-generated tasks rewarded for intermediate solver pass rate correspond to co-training a proposer against a solver.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: Domain card is flagged 'touches weights'; retention is weights, which places it outside harness scope.

claims.text: Matches or surpasses supervised search agents without curated QA data
claims.setting: Qwen2.5 3B/7B, Wikipedia E5 search, exact match, 7 QA sets
claims.baseline_control: Search-R1, R1, SFT, RAG, IRCoT, Search-o1, SQLM*, R-Zero*
claims.selection_vs_test: Test sets appear to be the standard public benchmarks; checkpoint selection per iteration not described as using held-out split
claims.result_denominator: avg EM 0.326/0.372; Table 10 gives ± across seeds for greedy decoding
claims.counterevidence: Search-R1 avg 0.327/0.384 is not exceeded on average; 7B MuSiQue 0.104 vs 0.168
claims.allowed_conclusion: Competitive with, not above, Search-R1 on average; weight-training result.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Weight-trained proposer-solver self-evolution reaches near-parity with supervised Search-R1 on short-form QA (author report).
